subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode incompatible cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice changes compatibility and session-retention behavior for existing users.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup semantics
options.body: Keep this direction, add persisted-row or doctor/update handling for omitted existing jobs, and reconcile the strict-validation PR around this contract.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the stricter validation path after its caller and recovery gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new default and document that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup semantics
recommendation.body: Keep this direction, add persisted-row or doctor/update handling for omitted existing jobs, and reconcile the strict-validation PR around this contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron store compatibility, doctor/runtime boundaries, and user-facing upgrade policy where recent path history shows the strongest ownership signal.
